chunks: Sa'd, from Abū Ja'far, from his father, from 'Abd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I asked Abū 'Abd Allāh عليه السلام about a place that had been a privy for a period of time, then it is cleaned and taken as a masjid. He said: Cast some soil over it until it is covered over, for that purifies it, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

key_terms.التُّرَابِ: soil or earth used here as a means of purification
key_terms.الْمَكَانِ: the place or site being discussed
key_terms.حَشًّا: a privy or place used for relieving oneself
key_terms.مَسْجِدًا: a masjid, a place designated for worship and sajdah
key_terms.يَتَوَارَى: to become concealed or covered over
key_terms.يُطَهِّرُهُ: purifies it; renders it ritually clean

ai.seo_question: How can a place that was formerly used as a privy be purified and made into a masjid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning a place formerly used as a privy that is later cleaned and made into a masjid. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that throwing soil over it until it is concealed serves as its purification, showing the legal effect of earth in restoring ritual suitability for worship.
